source.text: וַיָּקָם֩ אַחֲרֵ֨י אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְהוֹשִׁ֣יעַ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל תּוֹלָ֧ע בֶּן־פּוּאָ֛ה בֶּן־דּוֹד֖וֹ אִ֣ישׁ יִשָּׂשכָ֑ר וְהֽוּא־יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּשָׁמִ֖יר בְּהַ֥ר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose after Abimelech to save Israel Tola son of Puah son of Dodo, [a] man of Issachar; and he [was] living in Shamir in [the] hill country of Ephraim.

en.L: And after Abimelech there arose to save Israel Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar; and he was living in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
en.B: After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, rose up to save Israel. He was a man of Issachar, and he lived at Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
en.R: After Abimelech died, a man named Tola came forward to save Israel. He was the son of Puah and the grandson of Dodo, from the tribe of Issachar. He lived in the town of Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.

sw.L: Na baada ya Abimeleki akainuka Tola mwana wa Pua, mwana wa Dodo, mtu wa Isakari, ili kuwaokoa Israeli; naye alikuwa akikaa Shamiri katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu.
sw.B: Baada ya Abimeleki, Tola mwana wa Pua, mwana wa Dodo, aliinuka kuwaokoa Israeli. Alikuwa mtu wa Isakari, naye aliishi Shamiri katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu.
sw.R: Baada ya Abimeleki kufa, mtu mmoja aitwaye Tola alijitokeza kuwaokoa Israeli. Alikuwa mwana wa Pua na mjukuu wa Dodo, wa kabila la Isakari. Aliishi katika mji wa Shamiri katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu.

es.L: Y después de Abimelec se levantó para salvar a Israel Tola hijo de Fúa, hijo de Dodo, hombre de Isacar; y él habitaba en Samir, en la región montañosa de Efraín.
es.B: Después de Abimelec, Tola hijo de Fúa, hijo de Dodo, se levantó para salvar a Israel. Era un hombre de Isacar, y vivía en Samir, en la región montañosa de Efraín.
es.R: Después de que murió Abimelec, un hombre llamado Tola se levantó para salvar a Israel. Era hijo de Fúa y nieto de Dodo, de la tribu de Isacar. Vivía en la ciudad de Samir, en la región montañosa de Efraín.

fr.L: Et après Abimélek se leva, pour sauver Israël, Tola, fils de Poua, fils de Dodo, homme d’Issacar ; et il habitait à Shamir, dans la montagne d’Éphraïm.
fr.B: Après Abimélek, Tola, fils de Poua, fils de Dodo, se leva pour sauver Israël. C’était un homme d’Issacar, et il habitait à Shamir, dans la région montagneuse d’Éphraïm.
fr.R: Après la mort d’Abimélek, un homme appelé Tola s’est levé pour sauver Israël. Il était le fils de Poua et le petit-fils de Dodo, de la tribu d’Issacar. Il habitait la ville de Shamir, dans la région des collines d’Éphraïm.

vi.L: Và sau A-bi-mê-léc, Thô-la con trai Phu-a, con trai Đô-đô, người Y-sa-ca, dấy lên để giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên; và ông sống tại Sa-mia trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im.
vi.B: Sau A-bi-mê-léc, Thô-la con trai Phu-a, cháu Đô-đô, đứng lên giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ông là người Y-sa-ca và sống tại Sa-mia trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im.
vi.R: Sau khi A-bi-mê-léc chết, có một người tên là Thô-la đứng lên giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ông là con trai Phu-a và cháu Đô-đô, thuộc chi tộc Y-sa-ca. Ông sống tại thành Sa-mia trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im.

ko.L: 그리고 아비멜렉 뒤에 이스라엘을 구원하려고 잇사갈 사람, 도도의 손자이며 부아의 아들인 돌라가 일어났다. 그는 에브라임 산지 사밀에 살고 있었다.
ko.B: 아비멜렉 다음에는 도도의 손자이며 부아의 아들인 돌라가 일어나 이스라엘을 구했다. 그는 잇사갈 사람으로, 에브라임 산지의 사밀에 살았다.
ko.R: 아비멜렉이 죽은 뒤에 돌라라는 사람이 나서서 이스라엘을 구했다. 그는 부아의 아들이고 도도의 손자였으며, 잇사갈 지파 사람이었다. 그는 에브라임 산지의 사밀 성읍에 살았다.

pt.L: E depois de Abimeleque se levantou, para salvar Israel, Tola, filho de Puá, filho de Dodô, homem de Issacar; e ele morava em Samir, na região montanhosa de Efraim.
pt.B: Depois de Abimeleque, Tola, filho de Puá, filho de Dodô, se levantou para livrar Israel. Ele era um homem de Issacar e morava em Samir, na região montanhosa de Efraim.
pt.R: Depois que Abimeleque morreu, um homem chamado Tola se apresentou para livrar Israel. Ele era filho de Puá e neto de Dodô, da tribo de Issacar. Morava na cidade de Samir, na região montanhosa de Efraim.

am.L: ከአቢሜሌክም በኋላ እስራኤልን ለማዳን የይሳኮር ሰው፣ የዶዶ ልጅ የፉዋ ልጅ ቶላ ተነሣ፤ እርሱም በኮረብታማው የኤፍሬም አገር በሻሚር ይኖር ነበር።
am.B: ከአቢሜሌክ በኋላ የዶዶ ልጅ የፉዋ ልጅ ቶላ እስራኤልን ለማዳን ተነሣ። እርሱም የይሳኮር ሰው ነበረ፤ በኮረብታማው የኤፍሬም አገር በሻሚር ይኖር ነበር።
am.R: አቢሜሌክ ከሞተ በኋላ ቶላ የሚባል ሰው እስራኤልን ለማዳን ተነሣ። እርሱም የፉዋ ልጅ፣ የዶዶም የልጅ ልጅ ሲሆን ከይሳኮር ነገድ ነበረ። የሚኖረውም በኮረብታማው የኤፍሬም አገር በምትገኘው በሻሚር ከተማ ነበር።

decisions.choice: arose to save Israel: came forward as a rescuer
decisions.reason: The verb "save" is the one used of the judges the LORD raised up (2:16, 18; 3:9, 15). The text does not say whom Tola saved Israel from; after the ruin Abimelech brought on Shechem and Thebez (chapter 9), the rescue may have been from that disorder as much as from an outside enemy.

decisions.choice: Tola son of Puah, a man of Issachar: family names of Issachar
decisions.reason: Tola and Puah (also spelled Puvah) are the names of two of Issachar's sons (Genesis 46:13; Numbers 26:23; 1 Chronicles 7:1). This Tola carries old family names of his tribe.

decisions.choice: Dodo: a personal name
alternatives: son of Puah, son of his uncle
decisions.reason: The word is read as a name, as in 2 Samuel 23:9. The same letters could mean "his uncle", making Puah the uncle's son; the ancient Greek translation took it that way. As a list of fathers' names, a name fits best.

decisions.choice: a man of Issachar living in Shamir in Ephraim
decisions.reason: Issachar's land lay in the valley of Jezreel to the north (Joshua 19:17-23), but Tola lived in the hills of Ephraim, nearer the middle of the land. The site of Shamir is not known.

decisions.choice: Tola ... rose up / came forward; Readable "died", "grandson", "the town of"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the subject first. Readable says what "after Abimelech" means (after his death, 9:54-55), that "son of Dodo" here means grandson, and that Shamir is a town.

decisions.choice: "Tola hijo de Fúa, hijo de Dodo", "Samir"; later "Jair el galaadita", "Havot-jair", "Camón", "los maonitas", "Mizpa"
decisions.reason: Names in the usual Spanish forms; "Fúa" is the form of Genesis 46:13 and Numbers 26:23 for Issachar's son of the same name.

decisions.choice: "Tola", "Poua", "Dodo", "Shamir"; in this chapter also "Jaïr", "Havvoth-Jaïr", "Kamôn", "les Maonites", "Mitspa"
decisions.reason: For Judges 1-10: "Tola" and "Poua" are the forms already used for the sons of Issachar in the French Genesis 46; "Jaïr", "Havvoth-Jaïr" and "Mitspa" follow the French of Numbers, Deuteronomy and Genesis 31.

decisions.choice: the names of this chapter: "Thô-la", "Phu-a", "Đô-đô", "Sa-mia", "Giai-rơ", "Ha-vốt Giai-rơ", "Ca-môn", "Ma-ôn", "Mích-pa"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms, kept the same through the book; "Ga-la-át" for Gilead is the form the other Vietnamese books of this project use.

decisions.choice: "cháu Đô-đô" at Balanced
decisions.reason: Vietnamese says "cháu" (grandson) for the second "son of" in a line of descent, as the English Readable says "grandson"; Literal keeps "con trai".

decisions.choice: Tola, Puá, Dodô; Samir
decisions.reason: The two family names of Issachar (m2) keep the Portuguese of Genesis 46:13 for "Tola" and of Exodus 1:15 for "Puá", the spelling of the Hebrew here (Genesis 46:13 has the variant "Puva"); "Dodô" and "Samir" (as Joshua 15:48) are the usual Brazilian forms. "Salvar" (L) and "livrar" (B, R) follow 2:16.

records.literal_gloss: And he judged Israel twenty and three year[s], and he died and was buried in Shamir.

en.L: And he judged Israel twenty-three years, and he died and was buried in Shamir.
en.B: He judged Israel for twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried in Shamir.
en.R: Tola led Israel for twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried in Shamir.

sw.L: Naye akawaamua Israeli miaka ishirini na mitatu, akafa, akazikwa Shamiri.
sw.B: Aliwaamua Israeli kwa miaka ishirini na mitatu. Kisha akafa, akazikwa Shamiri.
sw.R: Tola aliwaongoza Israeli kwa miaka ishirini na mitatu. Kisha akafa, akazikwa Shamiri.

es.L: Y juzgó a Israel veintitrés años, y murió y fue sepultado en Samir.
es.B: Juzgó a Israel durante veintitrés años. Luego murió y fue sepultado en Samir.
es.R: Tola dirigió a Israel durante veintitrés años. Luego murió y fue sepultado en Samir.

fr.L: Et il jugea Israël vingt-trois ans, et il mourut et fut enterré à Shamir.
fr.B: Il jugea Israël pendant vingt-trois ans. Puis il mourut et fut enterré à Shamir.
fr.R: Tola a dirigé Israël pendant vingt-trois ans. Puis il est mort et il a été enterré à Shamir.

vi.L: Và ông xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên hai mươi ba năm, và ông qua đời và được chôn tại Sa-mia.
vi.B: Ông xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên trong hai mươi ba năm. Rồi ông qua đời và được chôn tại Sa-mia.
vi.R: Thô-la lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên trong hai mươi ba năm. Rồi ông qua đời và được chôn tại Sa-mia.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 이십삼 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스리다가 죽어서 사밀에 묻혔다.
ko.B: 그는 이십삼 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스렸다. 그러다가 죽어서 사밀에 묻혔다.
ko.R: 돌라는 이십삼 년 동안 이스라엘을 이끌었다. 그러다가 죽어서 사밀에 묻혔다.

pt.L: E ele julgou Israel vinte e três anos, e morreu, e foi sepultado em Samir.
pt.B: Ele julgou Israel durante vinte e três anos. Depois morreu e foi sepultado em Samir.
pt.R: Tola liderou Israel durante vinte e três anos. Depois morreu e foi enterrado em Samir.

am.L: እስራኤልንም ሃያ ሦስት ዓመት ዳኘ፤ ሞተም፤ በሻሚር ተቀበረ።
am.B: እስራኤልን ሃያ ሦስት ዓመት ዳኘ። ከዚያም ሞተ፤ በሻሚር ተቀበረ።

decisions.choice: judged Israel: led and governed Israel
decisions.reason: As at 2:16, a judge was a leader raised up to rescue Israel and govern it, more than a judge in a court.

decisions.choice: a short notice of a leader
decisions.reason: Tola and Jair (verses 3-5) are given only a few facts: where they came from, how long they led, and where they were buried. The same pattern returns for Ibzan, Elon and Abdon (12:8-15).

decisions.choice: led Israel
decisions.reason: As at 2:16: Readable says "led", since "judged" suggests only a court judge. Readable also names Tola as the subject.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘을 다스렸다" (L, B) and "이스라엘을 이끌었다" (R) for *shafat*
decisions.reason: As set at 3:10 for this block, following the terms of this translation for Judges.

decisions.choice: The minor judges' formula: "እስራኤልንም N ዓመት ዳኘ፤ ሞተም፤ በX ተቀበረ" (L); "እስራኤልን N ዓመት ዳኘ። ከዚያም ሞተ፤ በX ተቀበረ" (B); "እስራኤልን N ዓመት መራ። ከዚያም ሞተ፤ በX ተቀበረ" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is the one behind the title "judge", but here it means leading and governing (meaning decision m1), not only hearing cases. Literal and Balanced keep the judicial verb "ዳኘ", the verb behind the book's title "መሳፍንት"; Readable says "led", as the English does. The same wording is used for Jair (10:3), Jephthah (12:7), Ibzan, Elon and Abdon (12:8-15) and Samson (15:20; 16:31).

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם אַחֲרָ֔יו יָאִ֖יר הַגִּלְעָדִ֑י וַיִּשְׁפֹּט֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֖יִם שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose after him Jair the Gileadite, and he judged Israel twenty and two year[s].

en.L: And after him there arose Jair the Gileadite, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
en.B: After him came Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel for twenty-two years.
en.R: After Tola, a man named Jair came forward. He was from Gilead, and he led Israel for twenty-two years.

sw.L: Na baada yake akainuka Yairi Mgileadi, naye akawaamua Israeli miaka ishirini na miwili.
sw.B: Baada yake alikuja Yairi Mgileadi, aliyewaamua Israeli kwa miaka ishirini na miwili.
sw.R: Baada ya Tola, mtu mmoja aitwaye Yairi alijitokeza. Alitoka Gileadi, naye aliwaongoza Israeli kwa miaka ishirini na miwili.

es.L: Y después de él se levantó Jair el galaadita, y juzgó a Israel veintidós años.
es.B: Después de él vino Jair el galaadita, que juzgó a Israel durante veintidós años.
es.R: Después de Tola, se levantó un hombre llamado Jair. Era de Galaad, y dirigió a Israel durante veintidós años.

fr.L: Et après lui se leva Jaïr, le Galaadite, et il jugea Israël vingt-deux ans.
fr.B: Après lui vint Jaïr, le Galaadite, qui jugea Israël pendant vingt-deux ans.
fr.R: Après Tola, un homme appelé Jaïr s’est levé. Il venait de Galaad, et il a dirigé Israël pendant vingt-deux ans.

vi.L: Và sau ông, Giai-rơ người Ga-la-át dấy lên, và ông xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên hai mươi hai năm.
vi.B: Sau ông có Giai-rơ người Ga-la-át xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên trong hai mươi hai năm.
vi.R: Sau Thô-la, có một người tên là Giai-rơ đứng lên. Ông là người Ga-la-át, và ông lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên trong hai mươi hai năm.

ko.L: 그리고 그 뒤에 길르앗 사람 야일이 일어나서 이십이 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스렸다.
ko.B: 그 뒤를 이어 길르앗 사람 야일이 일어나 이십이 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스렸다.
ko.R: 돌라 다음에는 야일이라는 사람이 나섰다. 그는 길르앗 사람이었는데, 이십이 년 동안 이스라엘을 이끌었다.

pt.L: E depois dele se levantou Jair, o gileadita, e julgou Israel vinte e dois anos.
pt.B: Depois dele veio Jair, o gileadita, que julgou Israel durante vinte e dois anos.
pt.R: Depois de Tola, um homem chamado Jair se apresentou. Ele era de Gileade e liderou Israel durante vinte e dois anos.

am.L: ከእርሱም በኋላ ገለዓዳዊው ኢያዕር ተነሣ፤ እስራኤልንም ሃያ ሁለት ዓመት ዳኘ።
am.B: ከእርሱ በኋላ ገለዓዳዊው ኢያዕር ተነሣ፤ እርሱም እስራኤልን ሃያ ሁለት ዓመት ዳኘ።
am.R: ከቶላ በኋላ ኢያዕር የሚባል ሰው ተነሣ። እርሱም ከገለዓድ ነበረ፤ እስራኤልንም ሃያ ሁለት ዓመት መራ።

decisions.choice: Jair the Gileadite: from Gilead east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead was the hill country east of the Jordan, settled by Gad and half of Manasseh (Numbers 32:39-42). An earlier Jair of Manasseh had taken villages there and named them after himself (Numbers 32:41; Deuteronomy 3:14); this judge comes from the same region and bears the same name.

decisions.choice: led Israel; "He was from Gilead"
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, Readable says "led". It explains "the Gileadite" as "from Gilead".

decisions.choice: Jair, o gileadita
decisions.reason: "Jair" as Numbers 32:41 has the name in Portuguese, and "o gileadita" as 12:7 has it for Jephthah; Readable says "era de Gileade", as the English Readable explains the word.

records.literal_gloss: And were to him thirty sons riding on thirty male donkeys, and thirty towns [were] to them; to them they call Havvoth-jair until the day this, which [are] in [the] land of Gilead.

en.L: And he had thirty sons riding on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns; they call them Havvoth-jair to this day, which [are] in the land of Gilead.
en.B: Jair had thirty sons, riding thirty donkeys, and they owned thirty towns. Those towns in the land of Gilead are known as Havvoth-jair to this day.
en.R: Jair had thirty sons, and each one rode his own donkey and had his own town. These thirty towns are in the land of Gilead, and to this day people call them Havvoth-jair, which means "Jair's villages."

sw.L: Naye alikuwa na wana thelathini waliopanda punda thelathini, nao walikuwa na miji thelathini; wanaiita Havoth-yairi mpaka siku hii, [iliyo] katika nchi ya Gileadi.
sw.B: Yairi alikuwa na wana thelathini waliopanda punda thelathini, nao walimiliki miji thelathini. Miji hiyo iliyo katika nchi ya Gileadi inajulikana kwa jina la Havoth-yairi mpaka leo.
sw.R: Yairi alikuwa na wana thelathini, na kila mmoja alipanda punda wake mwenyewe na alikuwa na mji wake mwenyewe. Miji hiyo thelathini iko katika nchi ya Gileadi, na hata leo watu huiita Havoth-yairi, maana yake "Vijiji vya Yairi."

es.L: Y tuvo treinta hijos que cabalgaban sobre treinta asnos, y tenían treinta ciudades; las llaman Havot-jair hasta el día de hoy, las cuales [están] en la tierra de Galaad.
es.B: Jair tuvo treinta hijos, que montaban treinta asnos y poseían treinta ciudades. Esas ciudades de la tierra de Galaad se conocen hasta el día de hoy como Havot-jair.
es.R: Jair tuvo treinta hijos, y cada uno montaba su propio burro y tenía su propia ciudad. Estas treinta ciudades están en la tierra de Galaad, y hasta el día de hoy la gente las llama Havot-jair, que significa «las aldeas de Jair».

fr.L: Et il avait trente fils qui montaient trente ânons, et ils avaient trente villes ; on les appelle Havvoth-Jaïr jusqu’à ce jour, elles qui [sont] dans le pays de Galaad.
fr.B: Jaïr avait trente fils, qui montaient trente ânons et possédaient trente villes. Ces villes du pays de Galaad s’appellent encore aujourd’hui Havvoth-Jaïr.
fr.R: Jaïr avait trente fils, et chacun avait son âne et sa ville. Ces trente villes sont dans le pays de Galaad, et aujourd’hui encore, on les appelle Havvoth-Jaïr, ce qui veut dire « les villages de Jaïr ».

vi.L: Và ông có ba mươi con trai cưỡi trên ba mươi con lừa, và họ có ba mươi thành; người ta gọi chúng là Ha-vốt Giai-rơ cho đến ngày nay, [là các thành] ở trong xứ Ga-la-át.

vi.R: Giai-rơ có ba mươi con trai. Mỗi người cưỡi một con lừa riêng và có một thành riêng. Ba mươi thành này ở trong xứ Ga-la-át, và cho đến ngày nay người ta gọi chúng là Ha-vốt Giai-rơ, nghĩa là "Các làng của Giai-rơ".

ko.L: 그리고 그에게 서른 마리 나귀를 타는 아들 서른 명이 있었고, 그들에게 성읍 서른 개가 있었다. 사람들이 오늘까지 그것들을 하봇야일이라고 부르는데, 길르앗 땅에 [있다].

ko.R: 야일에게는 아들이 서른 명 있었다. 아들마다 자기 나귀를 타고 다녔고, 자기 성읍을 하나씩 가지고 있었다. 이 서른 성읍은 길르앗 땅에 있는데, 오늘날까지도 사람들은 그 성읍들을 '야일의 마을들'이라는 뜻의 하봇야일이라고 부른다.

pt.L: E ele tinha trinta filhos, que montavam em trinta jumentos, e eles tinham trinta cidades; a elas chamam Havote-Jair até este dia, as quais [estão] na terra de Gileade.
pt.B: Jair teve trinta filhos, que montavam trinta jumentos, e eles possuíam trinta cidades. Essas cidades, na terra de Gileade, são chamadas Havote-Jair até hoje.
pt.R: Jair teve trinta filhos, e cada um deles montava o seu próprio jumento e tinha a sua própria cidade. Essas trinta cidades ficam na terra de Gileade, e até hoje o povo as chama de Havote-Jair, que quer dizer "aldeias de Jair".

am.L: ሠላሳ አህዮችን የሚጋልቡ ሠላሳ ወንዶች ልጆችም ነበሩት፤ ለእነርሱም ሠላሳ ከተሞች ነበሯቸው፤ እስከ ዛሬ ድረስ ሐዎት ኢያዕር ብለው ይጠሯቸዋል፤ እነርሱም በገለዓድ ምድር [ያሉ ናቸው]።

am.R: ኢያዕር ሠላሳ ወንዶች ልጆች ነበሩት፤ እያንዳንዱም የራሱን አህያ ይጋልብ ነበር፤ የራሱም ከተማ ነበረው። እነዚህ ሠላሳ ከተሞች በገለዓድ ምድር ይገኛሉ፤ ሰዎችም እስከ ዛሬ ድረስ ሐዎት ኢያዕር ብለው ይጠሯቸዋል፤ ትርጉሙም «የኢያዕር መንደሮች» ማለት ነው።

decisions.choice: thirty donkeys ... thirty towns: a play on two words that sound alike
decisions.reason: The word for young male donkeys and the word for towns are written here with the same letters. The usual word for "towns" is a little different; it is spelled here to match "donkeys", so the line plays on the sound: thirty sons on thirty donkeys, with thirty towns.

decisions.choice: riding on donkeys: a mark of rank and wealth
decisions.reason: Leaders and their families rode donkeys (5:10; 12:14; 2 Samuel 16:2). Thirty sons each with his own mount and town show a large, wealthy household that governed a whole region.

decisions.choice: Havvoth-jair to this day: the villages of Jair
decisions.reason: The name means "the villages of Jair" or "Jair's tent villages". It is already given to villages in Gilead in Numbers 32:41 and Deuteronomy 3:14, and "to this day" shows that the narrator writes when the name was still in use.

decisions.choice: donkeys ... towns
decisions.reason: English has no pair of words that sound alike for donkeys and towns, so every level gives the plain sense, and a footnote points out the play on words. Readable adds what the name Havvoth-jair means and puts "each one" for the matching numbers.

decisions.choice: "treinta asnos ... treinta ciudades", without the wordplay
alternatives: a rhyme made up in Spanish
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the words for "donkeys" and "towns" sound almost alike (m1). Spanish cannot keep the play without changing the meaning, so it says plainly what the sons had, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "trente ânons ... trente villes"; the Hebrew play on two words that sound alike cannot be kept in French
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the words for "donkeys" and "towns" sound almost the same, as the meaning decision says. French has no pair that keeps both the sense and the sound, so it says what the words mean; "ânons", young male donkeys, keeps the Hebrew word's sense of a riding animal, a mark of rank.

decisions.choice: "lừa" and "thành"
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew the words for donkeys and for towns sound alike (m1); Vietnamese cannot keep the play, and says plainly what each word means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: the wordplay on "donkeys" and "towns" is not kept in Korean; "나귀" and "성읍" say the plain sense
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew words sound alike (m1); Korean has no pair of words that does the same, so the meaning decision tells the reader about the play.

decisions.choice: jumentos ... cidades; Havote-Jair
decisions.reason: Portuguese has no pair of like-sounding words for young donkeys and towns either, so every level gives the plain sense and the footnote tells the reader of the play on words (m1). "Havote-Jair" is the form Numbers 32:41 uses in Portuguese, and "até este dia" (L), "até hoje" (B, R) follow 1:21.

source.text: וַיֹּסִ֣פוּ׀בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הָרַע֮ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָה֒ וַיַּעַבְד֣וּ אֶת־הַבְּעָלִ֣ים וְאֶת־הָעַשְׁתָּר֡וֹת וְאֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲרָם֩ וְאֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֨י צִיד֜וֹן וְאֵ֣ת׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י מוֹאָ֗ב וְאֵת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י בְנֵי־עַמּ֔וֹן וְאֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּעַזְב֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א עֲבָדֽוּהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And added [the] sons of Israel to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and they served the Baals and the Ashtaroth and [the] gods of Aram and [the] gods of Sidon and [the] gods of Moab and [the] gods of [the] sons of Ammon and [the] gods of [the] Philistines; and they forsook Yahweh and not they served him.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel again did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Aram and the gods of Sidon and the gods of Moab and the gods of the sons of Ammon and the gods of the Philistines; and they forsook {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Once again the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and no longer served {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Once again the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. They worshiped the Baals and the goddesses called the Ashtaroth. They also worshiped the gods of the nations around them: Aram, Sidon, Moab, Ammon and Philistia. They turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and stopped serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakafanya tena maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakawatumikia Mabaali na Maashtorethi, na miungu ya Aramu, na miungu ya Sidoni, na miungu ya Moabu, na miungu ya wana wa Amoni, na miungu ya Wafilisti; wakamwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wala hawakumtumikia.
sw.B: Kwa mara nyingine Waisraeli walifanya maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Waliwatumikia Mabaali na Maashtorethi, miungu ya Aramu, miungu ya Sidoni, miungu ya Moabu, miungu ya Waamoni na miungu ya Wafilisti. Walimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wala hawakumtumikia tena.
sw.R: Kwa mara nyingine Waisraeli walifanya yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema ni maovu. Waliwaabudu Mabaali na miungu ya kike iitwayo Maashtorethi. Pia waliabudu miungu ya mataifa yaliyowazunguka: Aramu, Sidoni, Moabu, Amoni na Ufilisti. Walimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakaacha kumtumikia.

es.L: Y volvieron los hijos de Israel a hacer lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y sirvieron a los baales y a las astartés, y a los dioses de Aram, y a los dioses de Sidón, y a los dioses de Moab, y a los dioses de los hijos de Amón, y a los dioses de los filisteos; y abandonaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sirvieron.
es.B: Una vez más los israelitas hicieron lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Sirvieron a los baales y a las astartés, a los dioses de Aram, a los dioses de Sidón, a los dioses de Moab, a los dioses de los amonitas y a los dioses de los filisteos. Abandonaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y ya no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sirvieron.
es.R: Una vez más los israelitas hicieron lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho que era malo. Adoraron a los baales y a las diosas llamadas astartés. También adoraron a los dioses de las naciones que los rodeaban: Aram, Sidón, Moab, Amón y Filistea. Se apartaron {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y dejaron de servirle.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël firent encore le mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et ils servirent les Baals et les Astartés, et les dieux d’Aram, et les dieux de Sidon, et les dieux de Moab, et les dieux des fils d’Ammon, et les dieux des Philistins ; et ils abandonnèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servirent pas.
fr.B: Une fois encore, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} firent ce qui est mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Ils servirent les Baals et les Astartés, les dieux d’Aram, les dieux de Sidon, les dieux de Moab, les dieux des Ammonites et les dieux des Philistins. Ils abandonnèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servirent plus.
fr.R: Une fois encore, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont fait ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} déclarait mauvais. Ils ont adoré les Baals et les déesses qu’on appelle les Astartés. Ils ont aussi adoré les dieux des nations qui les entouraient : Aram, Sidon, Moab, Ammon et le pays des Philistins. Ils se sont détournés {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et ont arrêté de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servir.

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên lại làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và phụng sự các Ba-anh và các Át-tạt-tê, và các thần của A-ram, và các thần của Si-đôn, và các thần của Mô-áp, và các thần của con cái Am-môn, và các thần của người Phi-li-tin; và họ lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và không phụng sự {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên lại làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ phụng sự các thần Ba-anh và các nữ thần Át-tạt-tê, các thần của A-ram, các thần của Si-đôn, các thần của Mô-áp, các thần của người Am-môn và các thần của người Phi-li-tin. Họ lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và không còn phụng sự {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nữa.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên lại làm điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho là ác. Họ thờ các thần Ba-anh và các nữ thần gọi là Át-tạt-tê. Họ cũng thờ các thần của những dân tộc chung quanh: A-ram, Si-đôn, Mô-áp, Am-môn và Phi-li-tin. Họ quay lưng với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và thôi không phụng sự {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈에 악한 일을 했다. 그들은 바알들과 아스다롯과 아람의 신들과 시돈의 신들과 모압의 신들과 암몬 자손의 신들과 블레셋 사람들의 신들을 섬겼다. 그리고 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버리고 그분을 섬기지 않았다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성은 또다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 보시기에 악한 일을 했다. 그들은 바알들과 아스다롯, 그리고 아람의 신들, 시돈의 신들, 모압의 신들, 암몬 사람들의 신들, 블레셋 사람들의 신들을 섬겼다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버리고 더 이상 그분을 섬기지 않았다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성은 또다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 악하다고 하신 일을 했다. 그들은 바알들과, 아스다롯이라고 불리는 여신들을 섬겼다. 또 주위에 있는 아람, 시돈, 모압, 암몬, 블레셋 민족들의 신들도 섬겼다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 돌아서서 더 이상 주님을 섬기지 않았다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel voltaram a fazer o mal aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e serviram os baalins, e Astarote, e os deuses de Arã, e os deuses de Sidom, e os deuses de Moabe, e os deuses dos filhos de Amom, e os deuses dos filisteus; e abandonaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} e não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} serviram.
pt.B: Mais uma vez os israelitas fizeram o que era mau aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Serviram os baalins e Astarote, os deuses de Arã, os deuses de Sidom, os deuses de Moabe, os deuses dos amonitas e os deuses dos filisteus. Abandonaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} e deixaram de servi-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.
pt.R: Mais uma vez os israelitas fizeram o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} considerava mau. Eles adoraram os baalins e as várias formas da deusa Astarote. Adoraram também os deuses dos povos ao redor: de Arã, de Sidom, de Moabe, de Amom e da Filístia. Afastaram-se {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e deixaram de servi-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.

am.L: የእስራኤልም ልጆች ደግመው {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ዓይን ክፉ የሆነውን አደረጉ፤ በኣሊምንና አስታሮትን፣ የአራምን አማልክትና የሲዶናን አማልክት፣ የሞዓብን አማልክትና የአሞንን ልጆች አማልክት፣ የፍልስጥኤማውያንንም አማልክት አገለገሉ፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}}ም ተዉ፤ አላገለገሉትምም።
am.B: የእስራኤልም ልጆች እንደ ገና {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ክፉ የሆነውን አደረጉ። በኣሊምንና አስታሮትን፣ የአራምን፣ የሲዶናን፣ የሞዓብን፣ የአሞናውያንንና የፍልስጥኤማውያንን አማልክት አገለገሉ። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ተዉ፤ ከዚያ ወዲያም አላገለገሉትም።
am.R: እስራኤላውያን እንደ ገና {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ክፉ ነው የሚለውን አደረጉ። በኣሊምንና አስታሮት የተባሉትን ሴት አማልክት አመለኩ። በዙሪያቸው ያሉትን የአራምን፣ የሲዶናን፣ የሞዓብን፣ የአሞንንና የፍልስጥኤምን ሕዝቦች አማልክት ደግሞ አመለኩ። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ትተው ማገልገሉን አቆሙ።

decisions.choice: again did the evil in the eyes of the LORD: began the cycle once more
decisions.reason: "Added to do" means did again. The words open each new turn of the cycle in Judges: Israel sins, the LORD hands them over to enemies, they cry out, and he raises a rescuer (2:11-19; 3:7, 12; 4:1; 6:1; 13:1). Evil "in his eyes" is evil as the LORD judges it.

decisions.choice: the Baals and the Ashtaroth: the gods and goddesses of Canaan
decisions.reason: Baal was the Canaanite storm god, worshiped under many local names, so the plural means the Baal gods of many places; Ashtaroth is the plural of Ashtoreth (Astarte), a goddess of love and war. Together they stand for the whole of Canaanite worship (2:13; 1 Samuel 7:4; 12:10).

decisions.choice: seven groups of gods: worship of every neighbor's gods
decisions.reason: The list names seven kinds of gods, from Canaan, Aram to the north, Sidon on the coast, Moab and Ammon to the east and the Philistines to the west. It is the longest such list in the book: Israel took up the gods of every people around them. The LORD's answer in verses 11-12 names seven peoples he had saved them from.

decisions.choice: forsook the LORD and did not serve him: worship of him given up
decisions.reason: The last clause does not only say they added other gods. It says they left the LORD and stopped serving him, as 2:12-13 also says.

decisions.choice: the Baals and the goddesses called the Ashtaroth
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the names and says who the Ashtaroth were, as in 2:13. It joins the lists of nations in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: abandoned ... no longer served
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "abandoned" for the older "forsook" kept at Literal, and the same word in verses 10 and 13 where the Hebrew repeats the verb.

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L), os israelitas (B, R), with no gender setting
alternatives: os filhos e as filhas de Israel
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 and 6:1: "filhos" already takes in daughters and "os israelitas" names the whole people, so the English gender setting has nothing to change here or in the rest of chapters 10-11. The cycle's opening words and "os baalins", "Astarote" keep the wording 2:11-13 set for the book; "Arã" is the country of the "arameus" of Genesis 25:20.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun or gender spans in the Amharic of Judges 10: "የእስራኤል ልጆች" (R "እስራኤላውያን") for "the sons of Israel"
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God has nothing to change. "ልጆች" already includes daughters, so there is no second wording for the gender setting to switch to; the same through this chapter.

decisions.choice: The Judges refrain, as in Judges 1-5: "የእስራኤል ልጆች በእግዚአብሔር ዓይን ክፉ የሆነውን አደረጉ" (L), "... በእግዚአብሔር ፊት ክፉ የሆነውን አደረጉ" (B), "እስራኤላውያን እግዚአብሔር ክፉ ነው የሚለውን አደረጉ" (R); "again" is "ደግመው" (L), "እንደ ገና" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain that opens each cycle keeps one wording through the book (2:11; 3:7, 12; 4:1; 6:1; 10:6; 13:1). Literal keeps the Hebrew "eyes"; Balanced says "ፊት" (before), the ordinary Amharic idiom for doing something in someone's sight; Readable says what the LORD calls evil, as the English does.

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּמְכְּרֵם֙ בְּיַד־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּבְיַ֖ד בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh against Israel, and he sold them into [the] hand of [the] Philistines and into [the] hand of [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sold them into [the] hand of the Philistines and into [the] hand of the sons of Ammon.
en.B: Then the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blazed against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sold them into the power of the Philistines and into the power of the Ammonites.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became very angry with Israel. He handed them over to the Philistines and the Ammonites.

sw.L: Na hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawaka juu ya Israeli, akawauza mkononi mwa Wafilisti na mkononi mwa wana wa Amoni.
sw.B: Ndipo hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawaka dhidi ya Israeli, akawauza mikononi mwa Wafilisti na mikononi mwa Waamoni.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwakasirikia Israeli sana. Aliwatia mikononi mwa Wafilisti na Waamoni.

es.L: Y se encendió la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} contra Israel, y los vendió en mano de los filisteos y en mano de los hijos de Amón.
es.B: Entonces la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se encendió contra Israel, y los vendió en poder de los filisteos y en poder de los amonitas.
es.R: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó mucho con Israel. Los entregó a los filisteos y a los amonitas.

fr.L: Et la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflamma contre Israël, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les vendit dans la main des Philistins et dans la main des fils d’Ammon.
fr.B: Alors la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflamma contre Israël, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les vendit au pouvoir des Philistins et au pouvoir des Ammonites.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est mis très en colère contre Israël. Il les a livrés aux Philistins et aux Ammonites.

vi.L: Và cơn giận của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nổi phừng lên cùng Y-sơ-ra-ên, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bán họ vào tay người Phi-li-tin và vào tay con cái Am-môn.
vi.B: Bấy giờ cơn giận của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nổi phừng lên cùng Y-sơ-ra-ên, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bán họ vào tay người Phi-li-tin và người Am-môn.
vi.R: Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rất giận Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ngài giao họ cho người Phi-li-tin và người Am-môn.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 진노가 이스라엘에게 불타올라, 그분께서 그들을 블레셋 사람들의 손과 암몬 자손의 손에 파셨다.
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘에게 크게 진노하셔서, 그들을 블레셋 사람들과 암몬 사람들의 손에 파셨다.
ko.R: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 이스라엘에게 몹시 화가 나셨다. 주님께서는 그들을 블레셋 사람들과 암몬 사람들에게 넘기셨다.

pt.L: E a ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} se acendeu contra Israel, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os vendeu na mão dos filisteus e na mão dos filhos de Amom.
pt.B: Então a ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} se inflamou contra Israel, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os vendeu ao poder dos filisteus e ao poder dos amonitas.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ficou muito irado com Israel. Entregou os israelitas aos filisteus e aos amonitas, como um senhor vende um escravo.

am.L: {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}}ም ቁጣ በእስራኤል ላይ ነደደ፤ በፍልስጥኤማውያን እጅና በአሞን ልጆች እጅ ሸጣቸው።
am.B: በዚያን ጊዜ {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ቁጣ በእስራኤል ላይ ነደደ፤ በፍልስጥኤማውያንና በአሞናውያን እጅ ሸጣቸው።
am.R: ስለዚህ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} በእስራኤል ላይ እጅግ ተቆጣ፤ ለፍልስጥኤማውያንና ለአሞናውያን አሳልፎ ሰጣቸው።

decisions.choice: the anger burned: he was very angry
decisions.reason: Hebrew speaks of anger as burning or growing hot (2:14, 20; 3:8).

decisions.choice: sold them into the hand of: handed them over to the power of
decisions.reason: "Selling" people into an enemy's hand means giving them up to that enemy's control (2:14; 3:8; 4:2). The "hand" is power.

decisions.choice: the Philistines and the Ammonites: enemies on two sides
decisions.reason: The Philistines pressed on Israel from the coast in the west, the Ammonites from the east across the Jordan. The Ammonite threat is told first (10:8-12:7, Jephthah); the Philistine one comes later (chapters 13-16, Samson).

decisions.choice: handed them over to
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of selling into someone's hand, as in 3:8 and 4:2; Balanced keeps "sold ... into the power of".

decisions.choice: os filhos de Amom (L); os amonitas (B, R)
decisions.reason: For chapters 10-11, as 12:1 and Numbers 21:24 have it in Portuguese: Literal keeps the Hebrew "sons of Ammon", Balanced and Readable say "os amonitas". The selling keeps the wording 2:14 set for the book.

source.text: וַֽיִּרְעֲצ֤וּ וַיְרֹֽצְצוּ֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִ֑יא שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֜ה שָׁנָ֗ה אֶֽת־כָּל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּגִּלְעָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And they shattered and crushed [the] sons of Israel in the year that, eighteen year[s], all [the] sons of Israel who [were] across the Jordan in [the] land of the Amorite[s], which [is] in Gilead.

en.L: And they shattered and crushed the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel in that year; for eighteen years [they did so to] all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel who [were] across the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which [is] in Gilead.
en.B: That year they shattered and crushed the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and for eighteen years they oppressed all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who lived east of the Jordan in Gilead, the land of the Amorites.
en.R: That year they began to crush the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and treat them harshly. For eighteen years they did this to all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who lived east of the Jordan River, in Gilead, where the Amorites used to live.

sw.L: Nao wakawavunja na kuwaponda wana wa Israeli mwaka ule; kwa miaka kumi na minane [waliwatendea hivyo] wana wote wa Israeli [waliokuwa] ng'ambo ya Yordani katika nchi ya Waamori, [iliyo] katika Gileadi.
sw.B: Mwaka ule waliwavunja na kuwaponda Waisraeli, na kwa miaka kumi na minane waliwaonea Waisraeli wote walioishi mashariki ya Yordani katika Gileadi, nchi ya Waamori.
sw.R: Mwaka ule walianza kuwaponda Waisraeli na kuwatendea kwa ukatili. Kwa miaka kumi na minane waliwatendea hivyo Waisraeli wote walioishi mashariki ya Mto Yordani, katika Gileadi, walikoishi Waamori zamani.

es.L: Y quebrantaron y oprimieron a los hijos de Israel en aquel año; dieciocho años [lo hicieron] a todos los hijos de Israel que [estaban] al otro lado del Jordán, en la tierra de los amorreos, que [está] en Galaad.
es.B: Aquel año quebrantaron y aplastaron a los israelitas, y durante dieciocho años oprimieron a todos los israelitas que vivían al este del Jordán, en Galaad, la tierra de los amorreos.
es.R: Aquel año comenzaron a aplastar a los israelitas y a tratarlos con dureza. Durante dieciocho años hicieron esto a todos los israelitas que vivían al este del río Jordán, en Galaad, donde antes vivían los amorreos.

fr.L: Et ils brisèrent et écrasèrent les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël cette année-là ; pendant dix-huit ans [ils traitèrent ainsi] tous les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël qui [étaient] au-delà du Jourdain, dans le pays des Amoréens, qui [est] en Galaad.
fr.B: Cette année-là, ils brisèrent et écrasèrent les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, et pendant dix-huit ans, ils opprimèrent tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} qui vivaient à l’est du Jourdain, en Galaad, le pays des Amoréens.
fr.R: Cette année-là, ils ont commencé à écraser les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} et à les maltraiter. Pendant dix-huit ans, ils ont fait cela à tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} qui vivaient à l’est du fleuve Jourdain, en Galaad, là où vivaient autrefois les Amoréens.

vi.L: Và chúng đập tan và nghiền nát con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên trong năm ấy; trong mười tám năm [chúng làm như vậy với] tất cả con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên ở bên kia sông Giô-đanh, trong xứ của người A-mô-rít, [là xứ] ở Ga-la-át.
vi.B: Năm ấy chúng đập tan và nghiền nát dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, và trong mười tám năm chúng áp bức tất cả dân Y-sơ-ra-ên sống ở phía đông sông Giô-đanh, tại Ga-la-át, xứ của người A-mô-rít.
vi.R: Năm ấy chúng bắt đầu chà đạp và hành hạ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Trong mười tám năm, chúng làm như vậy với tất cả dân Y-sơ-ra-ên sống ở phía đông sông Giô-đanh, tại Ga-la-át, là nơi người A-mô-rít trước kia sinh sống.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그해에 이스라엘 자손을 부수고 짓밟았다. 십팔 년 동안 요단강 건너편 길르앗에 있는 아모리 사람들의 땅에 [있는] 모든 이스라엘 자손에게 [그렇게 하였다].
ko.B: 그해에 그들은 이스라엘 백성을 부수고 짓밟았다. 그리고 십팔 년 동안 요단강 동쪽, 아모리 사람들의 땅인 길르앗에 사는 모든 이스라엘 백성을 억눌렀다.
ko.R: 그해에 그들은 이스라엘 백성을 짓밟고 모질게 괴롭히기 시작했다. 그들은 십팔 년 동안 요단강 동쪽 길르앗에 사는 모든 이스라엘 백성을 그렇게 괴롭혔다. 그곳은 전에 아모리 사람들이 살던 땅이었다.

pt.L: E eles despedaçaram e esmagaram os filhos de Israel naquele ano; durante dezoito anos [fizeram isso a] todos os filhos de Israel que [estavam] além do Jordão, na terra dos amorreus, que [está] em Gileade.
pt.B: Naquele ano eles despedaçaram e esmagaram os israelitas, e durante dezoito anos oprimiram todos os israelitas que viviam a leste do Jordão, em Gileade, a terra dos amorreus.
pt.R: Naquele ano eles começaram a esmagar os israelitas e a maltratá-los. Durante dezoito anos fizeram isso com todos os israelitas que moravam a leste do rio Jordão, em Gileade, onde antes moravam os amorreus.

am.L: እነርሱም በዚያ ዓመት የእስራኤልን ልጆች ሰባበሩ፤ አደቀቁም፤ በዮርዳኖስ ማዶ በገለዓድ ባለው በአሞራውያን ምድር የነበሩትን የእስራኤልን ልጆች ሁሉ አሥራ ስምንት ዓመት [እንዲሁ አደረጉባቸው]።
am.B: በዚያ ዓመት የእስራኤልን ልጆች ሰባበሩ፤ አደቀቁም፤ ከዮርዳኖስ በስተ ምሥራቅ በአሞራውያን ምድር በገለዓድ የሚኖሩትን የእስራኤልን ልጆች ሁሉ አሥራ ስምንት ዓመት አስጨነቁ።
am.R: በዚያ ዓመት እስራኤላውያንን ማድቀቅና በጭካኔ መግዛት ጀመሩ። ከዮርዳኖስ ወንዝ በስተ ምሥራቅ፣ ቀድሞ አሞራውያን ይኖሩበት በነበረው በገለዓድ የሚኖሩትን እስራኤላውያን ሁሉ አሥራ ስምንት ዓመት እንዲህ አደረጓቸው።

decisions.choice: shattered and crushed: two words of breaking, used together
decisions.reason: The two verbs sound alike and both mean to break or crush. Together they stress how hard the oppression was. The same pair describes the fate of a disobedient Israel in Deuteronomy 28:33.

decisions.choice: in that year ... eighteen years: it began that year and lasted eighteen
decisions.reason: The sentence is compressed: the attack began "in that year", and for eighteen years it went on against the Israelites east of the Jordan. The second part has no verb of its own; it takes its sense from the first.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan in the land of the Amorites in Gilead
decisions.reason: "Across the Jordan" is seen from the land west of the river, so it means east of it. This region had been the land of the Amorite king Sihon before Israel took it (Numbers 21:21-31), and it bordered Ammon.

decisions.choice: Literal "[they did so to]"; Balanced "they oppressed"; Readable "they did this to"
decisions.reason: English needs a verb for the second half of the sentence. Every level supplies one from the first half; Literal puts it in brackets. Readable says "used to live" because by now Israel held the land.

source.text: וַיַּעַבְר֤וּ בְנֵֽי־עַמּוֹן֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לְהִלָּחֵ֛ם גַּם־בִּיהוּדָ֥ה וּבְבִנְיָמִ֖ין וּבְבֵ֣ית אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַתֵּ֥צֶר לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And crossed [the] sons of Ammon the Jordan to fight also against Judah and against Benjamin and against [the] house of Ephraim; and it was distress to Israel greatly.

en.L: And the sons of Ammon crossed the Jordan to fight also against Judah and against Benjamin and against the house of Ephraim; and Israel was in great distress.
en.B: The Ammonites even crossed the Jordan to make war on Judah, on Benjamin and on the house of Ephraim. Israel was in great distress.
en.R: The Ammonites even crossed the Jordan River to fight against the tribes of Judah, Benjamin and Ephraim. Israel was in terrible trouble.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Amoni wakavuka Yordani ili kupigana pia na Yuda, na Benyamini, na nyumba ya Efraimu; naye Israeli akawa katika dhiki kubwa.
sw.B: Waamoni walivuka hata Yordani ili kupigana na Yuda, Benyamini na nyumba ya Efraimu. Israeli walikuwa katika dhiki kubwa.
sw.R: Waamoni walivuka hata Mto Yordani ili kupigana na makabila ya Yuda, Benyamini na Efraimu. Israeli walikuwa katika taabu kubwa sana.

es.L: Y los hijos de Amón pasaron el Jordán para pelear también contra Judá, y contra Benjamín, y contra la casa de Efraín; e Israel estuvo en gran angustia.
es.B: Los amonitas incluso cruzaron el Jordán para hacer la guerra a Judá, a Benjamín y a la casa de Efraín. Israel estaba en gran angustia.
es.R: Los amonitas incluso cruzaron el río Jordán para pelear contra las tribus de Judá, Benjamín y Efraín. Israel estaba en un terrible aprieto.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Ammon passèrent le Jourdain pour combattre aussi contre Juda, et contre Benjamin, et contre la maison d’Éphraïm ; et Israël fut dans une grande détresse.
fr.B: Les Ammonites passèrent même le Jourdain pour faire la guerre à Juda, à Benjamin et à la maison d’Éphraïm. Israël fut dans une grande détresse.
fr.R: Les Ammonites ont même traversé le fleuve Jourdain pour combattre les tribus de Juda, de Benjamin et d’Éphraïm. Israël était dans une situation terrible.

vi.L: Và con cái Am-môn vượt qua sông Giô-đanh để đánh cả Giu-đa, Bên-gia-min và nhà Ép-ra-im nữa; và Y-sơ-ra-ên bị khốn đốn lắm.
vi.B: Người Am-môn còn vượt qua sông Giô-đanh để tấn công Giu-đa, Bên-gia-min và nhà Ép-ra-im. Y-sơ-ra-ên lâm vào cảnh vô cùng khốn đốn.
vi.R: Người Am-môn còn vượt qua sông Giô-đanh để đánh các chi tộc Giu-đa, Bên-gia-min và Ép-ra-im. Y-sơ-ra-ên gặp hoạn nạn khủng khiếp.

ko.L: 그리고 암몬 자손이 요단강을 건너 유다와 베냐민과 에브라임 집과도 싸웠다. 그래서 이스라엘이 몹시 괴로웠다.
ko.B: 암몬 사람들은 요단강을 건너와서 유다와 베냐민과 에브라임 집안까지 쳤다. 이스라엘은 큰 고통에 빠졌다.
ko.R: 암몬 사람들은 요단강을 건너와서 유다 지파와 베냐민 지파와 에브라임 지파까지 공격했다. 이스라엘은 큰 어려움에 빠졌다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Amom atravessaram o Jordão para lutar também contra Judá, e contra Benjamim, e contra a casa de Efraim; e Israel ficou em grande angústia.
pt.B: Os amonitas chegaram a atravessar o Jordão para guerrear contra Judá, contra Benjamim e contra a casa de Efraim. Israel ficou em grande aflição.
pt.R: Os amonitas chegaram até a atravessar o rio Jordão para lutar contra as tribos de Judá, de Benjamim e de Efraim. Israel ficou numa situação terrível.

am.L: የአሞንም ልጆች ከይሁዳና ከብንያም ከኤፍሬምም ቤት ጋር ደግሞ ሊዋጉ ዮርዳኖስን ተሻገሩ፤ እስራኤልም እጅግ ተጨነቀ።
am.B: አሞናውያንም ይሁዳን፣ ብንያምንና የኤፍሬምን ቤት ለመውጋት ዮርዳኖስን እንኳ ተሻገሩ። እስራኤልም በታላቅ ጭንቅ ውስጥ ነበረ።
am.R: አሞናውያን የይሁዳን፣ የብንያምንና የኤፍሬምን ነገዶች ለመውጋት የዮርዳኖስን ወንዝ እንኳ ተሻገሩ። እስራኤልም እጅግ በከፋ ችግር ውስጥ ወደቀ።

decisions.choice: Judah, Benjamin and Ephraim: the tribes west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The Ammonites did not stop at Gilead. They crossed the river into the central and southern hill country, the heart of Israel's land.

decisions.choice: it was distress to Israel greatly: Israel was hard pressed
decisions.reason: The verb means to be tight or narrow, a picture of being hemmed in. It is used of Israel's trouble in 2:15.

decisions.choice: the tribes of; "even"
decisions.reason: Readable names these as tribes, and "even" shows that the attack had spread beyond the east side of the river.

source.text: וַֽיִּזְעֲקוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר חָטָ֣אנוּ לָ֔ךְ וְכִ֤י עָזַ֨בְנוּ֙ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ וַֽנַּעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־הַבְּעָלִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And cried out [the] sons of Israel to Yahweh, saying, we have sinned against you, and indeed we have forsaken our God and we have served the Baals.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "We have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for we have forsaken our God and served the Baals."
en.B: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "We have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because we have abandoned our God and served the Baals."
en.R: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help. They said, "We have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. We turned away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, our God, and worshiped the Baals."

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakisema, "Tumetenda dhambi dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, kwa maana tumemwacha Mungu wetu na kuwatumikia Mabaali."
sw.B: Ndipo Waisraeli walimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Tumetenda dhambi dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, kwa sababu tumemwacha Mungu wetu na kuwatumikia Mabaali."
sw.R: Ndipo Waisraeli walimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awasaidie. Walisema, "Tumetenda dhambi dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. Tumekuacha {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Mungu wetu, tukawaabudu Mabaali."

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, diciendo: «Hemos pecado contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, porque hemos abandonado a nuestro Dios y hemos servido a los baales.»
es.B: Entonces los israelitas clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Hemos pecado contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, porque hemos abandonado a nuestro Dios y hemos servido a los baales.»
es.R: Entonces los israelitas clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} pidiendo ayuda. Dijeron: «Hemos pecado contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Nos apartamos de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, nuestro Dios, y adoramos a los baales.»

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël crièrent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, en disant : « Nous avons péché contre {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, car nous avons abandonné notre Dieu et nous avons servi les Baals. »
fr.B: Alors les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} crièrent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Nous avons péché contre {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, car nous avons abandonné notre Dieu et servi les Baals. »
fr.R: Alors les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont appelé {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au secours. Ils ont dit : « Nous avons péché contre {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Nous {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons abandonné, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, notre Dieu, et nous avons adoré les Baals. »

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rằng: "Chúng con đã phạm tội cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì chúng con đã lìa bỏ Đức Chúa Trời của chúng con và phụng sự các Ba-anh."
vi.B: Bấy giờ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Chúng con đã phạm tội cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì chúng con đã lìa bỏ Đức Chúa Trời của chúng con mà phụng sự các thần Ba-anh."
vi.R: Bấy giờ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ. Họ nói: "Chúng con đã phạm tội cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Chúng con đã quay lưng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là Đức Chúa Trời của chúng con, mà thờ các thần Ba-anh."

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖어 말했다. "우리가 주님께 죄를 지었습니다. 우리가 우리 하나님을 버리고 바알들을 섬겼습니다."
ko.B: 그러자 이스라엘 백성이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다. "우리가 주님께 죄를 지었습니다. 우리 하나님을 버리고 바알들을 섬겼습니다."
ko.R: 그러자 이스라엘 백성이 도와 달라고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다. "우리가 주님께 죄를 지었습니다. 우리 하나님이신 주님을 떠나 바알들을 섬겼습니다."

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, dizendo: "Pecamos contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, pois abandonamos o nosso Deus e servimos os baalins."
pt.B: Então os israelitas clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Pecamos contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, porque abandonamos o nosso Deus e servimos os baalins."
pt.R: Então os israelitas clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, pedindo socorro. Eles disseram: "Pecamos contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Nós nos afastamos de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, o nosso Deus, e adoramos os baalins."

am.L: የእስራኤልም ልጆች {{divine_name:ወደ እግዚአብሔር|ወደ ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ብለው ጮኹ፦ «አንተን በድለናል፤ አምላካችንን ትተናልና፤ በኣሊምንም አገልግለናል።»
am.B: የእስራኤልም ልጆች {{divine_name:ወደ እግዚአብሔር|ወደ ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ብለው ጮኹ፦ «አምላካችንን ትተን በኣሊምን ስላገለገልን አንተን በድለናል።»
am.R: እስራኤላውያንም ርዳታ ለማግኘት {{divine_name:ወደ እግዚአብሔር|ወደ ያህዌ}} ጮኹ፤ እንዲህም አሉ፦ «አንተን በድለናል። አምላካችን የሆንከውን አንተን ትተን በኣሊምን አመለክን።»

decisions.choice: cried out: the call for help that turns each cycle
decisions.reason: Israel's cry to the LORD comes at the low point of each cycle (3:9, 15; 4:3; 6:6-7). This time, for the first time in the book, the cry includes a confession of sin.

decisions.choice: and indeed we have forsaken: the confession names the sin
decisions.reason: The small word can mean "because" or simply stress what follows ("indeed"). Either way the second clause says what the sin was: leaving their own God for the Baals.

decisions.choice: for help; "you, our God"
decisions.reason: Readable says that the cry was a call for help. Since the people are speaking to the LORD, it says "turned away from you, our God", which keeps the sense of "forsaken our God".

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to [the] sons of Israel, [did I] not from Egypt and from the Amorite[s] and from [the] sons of Ammon and from [the] Philistines

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, "[Did I] not [save you] from Egypt and from the Amorites and from the sons of Ammon and from the Philistines?
en.B: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "Did I not save you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites and the Philistines?
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "Remember how I saved you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites and the Philistines.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawaambia wana wa Israeli, "Je, [sikuwaokoa] kutoka Misri, na kutoka kwa Waamori, na kutoka kwa wana wa Amoni, na kutoka kwa Wafilisti?
sw.B: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaambia Waisraeli, "Je, sikuwaokoa kutoka kwa Wamisri, Waamori, Waamoni na Wafilisti?
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwajibu Waisraeli, "Kumbukeni jinsi nilivyowaokoa kutoka kwa Wamisri, Waamori, Waamoni na Wafilisti.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a los hijos de Israel: «¿No [{{plural_you:los|os}} salvé yo] de Egipto, y de los amorreos, y de los hijos de Amón, y de los filisteos?

es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les respondió a los israelitas: «{{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} cómo {{plural_you:los|os}} salvé de los egipcios, de los amorreos, de los amonitas y de los filisteos.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël : « [Ne vous ai-je] pas [sauvés] de l’Égypte, et des Amoréens, et des fils d’Ammon, et des Philistins ?
fr.B: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : « Ne vous ai-je pas sauvés des Égyptiens, des Amoréens, des Ammonites et des Philistins ?
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : « Souvenez-vous : je vous ai sauvés des Égyptiens, des Amoréens, des Ammonites et des Philistins.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên: "[Chẳng phải Ta đã cứu các ngươi] khỏi Ai Cập, khỏi người A-mô-rít, khỏi con cái Am-môn và khỏi người Phi-li-tin sao?
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với dân Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Chẳng phải Ta đã cứu các ngươi khỏi người Ai Cập, người A-mô-rít, người Am-môn và người Phi-li-tin sao?
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp lời dân Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Hãy nhớ lại Ta đã cứu các ngươi khỏi người Ai Cập, người A-mô-rít, người Am-môn và người Phi-li-tin thế nào.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 자손에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 이집트와 아모리 사람들과 암몬 자손과 블레셋 사람들에게서 [너희를 구원하지] 않았느냐?
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 백성에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 너희를 이집트 사람들과 아모리 사람들과 암몬 사람들과 블레셋 사람들에게서 구해 주지 않았느냐?
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 백성에게 대답하셨다. "내가 이집트 사람들과 아모리 사람들과 암몬 사람들과 블레셋 사람들에게서 너희를 구해 준 일을 기억하여라.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse aos filhos de Israel: "Não [salvei eu vocês] do Egito, e dos amorreus, e dos filhos de Amom, e dos filisteus?
pt.B: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse aos israelitas: "Não fui eu que salvei vocês dos egípcios, dos amorreus, dos amonitas e dos filisteus?
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu aos israelitas: "Lembrem-se de como eu salvei vocês dos egípcios, dos amorreus, dos amonitas e dos filisteus.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም ለእስራኤል ልጆች እንዲህ አለ፦ «ከግብፅና ከአሞራውያን፣ ከአሞን ልጆችና ከፍልስጥኤማውያን [ያዳንኳችሁ እኔ] አይደለሁምን?
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም ለእስራኤል ልጆች እንዲህ አለ፦ «ከግብፃውያን፣ ከአሞራውያን፣ ከአሞናውያንና ከፍልስጥኤማውያን ያዳንኳችሁ እኔ አይደለሁምን?

decisions.choice: the question breaks off: "Did I not save you from ...?"
alternatives: read verses 11-12 as one long sentence: "Was it not from Egypt ... and the Sidonians ... oppressed you, and I saved you?"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins a question, "Was it not from Egypt and from the Amorites ...", and does not finish it; verse 12 goes on with more names and ends with "I saved you from their hand". The sense of the whole is "Did I not save you from all of these?" The broken sentence may show the force of the LORD's reply.

decisions.choice: Egypt, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines: past rescues
decisions.reason: Egypt recalls the exodus; the Amorites, Israel's victories over Sihon and Og (Numbers 21:21-35); the Ammonites, the war of Eglon king of Moab with Ammon at his side (3:13); the Philistines, Shamgar's victory (3:31).

decisions.choice: Literal "[Did I] not [save you]"; Balanced "Did I not save you"; Readable "Remember how I saved you"
decisions.reason: English cannot leave the question unfinished and still be clear, so every level supplies "save you" from verse 12; Literal puts the supplied words in brackets. Readable turns the question into the statement it expects.

decisions.choice: the LORD calls Israel "các ngươi"
decisions.reason: As at 2:1: a rebuke to a people who have forsaken him; "các ngươi" keeps its weight.

decisions.choice: vocês (the LORD to Israel, verses 11-14); salvei vocês
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks to Israel in the plural, so Portuguese says "vocês", as 2:1 and 6:8 set it; like 6:8, it writes "salvei vocês" rather than "os salvei", which could be taken for the enemies just named.

records.literal_gloss: and [the] Sidonians and Amalek and Maon oppressed you, and you cried out to me, and I saved you from their hand.

en.R: When the Sidonians, the Amalekites and the Maonites treated you cruelly, you cried out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I saved you from them.

es.B: Cuando los sidonios, los amalecitas y los maonitas {{plural_you:los|os}} oprimieron y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:clamaron|clamasteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, yo {{plural_you:los|os}} salvé de su poder.

fr.L: Et les Sidoniens, et Amalek, et Maôn vous ont opprimés, et vous avez crié vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et je vous ai sauvés de leur main.
fr.B: Quand les Sidoniens, les Amalécites et les Maonites vous ont opprimés et que vous avez crié vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous ai sauvés de leur pouvoir.
fr.R: Quand les Sidoniens, les Amalécites et les Maonites vous ont maltraités, vous avez crié vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et je vous ai sauvés de leurs mains.

vi.L: Và người Si-đôn, A-ma-léc và Ma-ôn đã áp bức các ngươi, và các ngươi kêu cầu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và Ta đã cứu các ngươi khỏi tay chúng.

decisions.choice: Maon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "Maon", a people of the south also named among Israel's enemies in 2 Chronicles 26:7 (Meunites). Many manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation read "Midian", which would recall Gideon's war (chapters 6-8). The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: seven peoples: the LORD's record of rescue
decisions.reason: With verse 11 the LORD names seven peoples he saved Israel from, matching the seven groups of gods Israel served in verse 6. Not every one of these rescues is told in Judges; the list sums up the LORD's faithfulness against Israel's unfaithfulness.

decisions.choice: from their hand: from their power
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, the "hand" is the power of the enemy.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites and the Maonites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the peoples by the usual English forms for them; Literal keeps "Amalek" and "Maon" as the Hebrew has them.

decisions.choice: os sidônios; Amaleque, Maom (L); os amalequitas, os maonitas (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Sidônios" and "amalequitas" are the forms of Deuteronomy 3:9 and Genesis 14:7 in Portuguese; "Maom" is written as the town of Joshua 15:55. Literal keeps the names of the peoples as the Hebrew has them, as the English does.

ko.L: 그런데 너희는 나를 버리고 다른 신들을 섬겼다. 그러므로 내가 다시는 너희를 구원하지 않겠다.

pt.L: Mas vocês, vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} abandonaram e serviram outros deuses; por isso não voltarei a salvar vocês.

pt.R: Mas vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deixaram e adoraram outros deuses. Por isso eu não vou mais salvar vocês.

decisions.choice: and you, you: stress on Israel's part
decisions.reason: The extra word "you" sets Israel's conduct against what the LORD had done in verses 11-12: he saved, but they left him.

decisions.choice: I will not again save you: a real refusal, not the last word
decisions.reason: The LORD refuses to rescue them again, as a judgment on their repeated turning away. Verse 16 shows that the story does not end there, and 11:29-33 tells of the rescue that followed.

decisions.choice: will not add: will not do again
decisions.reason: The verb is the one that opened the cycle in verse 6: Israel "added" to do evil, and now the LORD will not "add" to save them.

en.L: Go and cry out to the gods whom you have chosen; let them save you in the time of your distress."
en.B: Go and cry to the gods you chose for yourselves. Let them be the ones to save you when trouble comes."
en.R: Go and cry out for help to the gods you chose! Let them save you from your trouble."

sw.R: Nendeni mkaililie msaada miungu mliyoichagua! Hiyo na iwaokoe katika taabu yenu."

es.B: {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:clamen|clamad}} a los dioses que {{plural_you:escogieron|escogisteis}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Que sean ellos los que {{plural_you:los|os}} salven cuando llegue la angustia.»

vi.B: Hãy đi kêu cầu các thần các ngươi đã chọn cho mình. Hãy để chính chúng cứu các ngươi khi hoạn nạn đến."
vi.R: Hãy đi kêu cầu các thần các ngươi đã chọn mà xin chúng giúp đỡ! Hãy để chúng cứu các ngươi khỏi hoạn nạn!"

ko.B: 가서 너희가 스스로 택한 신들에게 부르짖어라. 너희가 어려움을 당할 때에 그 신들이 너희를 구해 주게 하여라."
ko.R: 가서 너희가 고른 신들에게 도와 달라고 부르짖어라! 너희가 어려움을 당할 때에 그 신들이 너희를 구해 주라고 하여라."

pt.B: Vão clamar aos deuses que vocês escolheram para si. Que eles salvem vocês quando a aflição chegar."
pt.R: Vão pedir socorro aos deuses que vocês escolheram! Que eles salvem vocês dos seus problemas."

am.B: ሂዱ፤ ለራሳችሁ ወደ መረጣችኋቸው አማልክት ጩኹ። በመከራችሁ ጊዜ የሚያድኗችሁ እነርሱ ይሁኑ።»
am.R: ሂዱ፤ ርዳታ ለማግኘት ወደ መረጣችኋቸው አማልክት ጩኹ! እነርሱ ከችግራችሁ ያድኗችሁ።»

decisions.choice: go and cry out ... let them save you: a challenge with bitter irony
decisions.reason: The commands are not real instructions to pray to other gods. They show that those gods cannot help, since they had never saved Israel (compare Deuteronomy 32:37-38; Jeremiah 2:28).

decisions.choice: the gods you have chosen: worship as a choice
decisions.reason: Israel had once chosen to serve the LORD (Joshua 24:15, 22). Now the LORD says they have chosen other gods, and must face what that choice brings.

decisions.choice: cry out for help
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, Readable says that the cry is a call for help, and an exclamation mark gives the tone of the challenge.
